page: Amazon Web Services i4i.32xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs derived from 64 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8375C processor operating at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. A key hardware feature is the inclusion of 30,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 123,862.56 and a top-tier Passmark CPU score of 86,632.57. The processor's cryptographic capabilities are highlighted by a top-tier Passmark CPU encryption test score of 110,454.76, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instructions. Memory performance is robust, showing a read-only large block bandwidth of 333.72 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, as demonstrated by a strong Passmark database score of 29,745.24 and Redis SET operations reaching 104.77 million operations per second. However, without dedicated GPU hardware, large-scale LLM text generation is a performance bottleneck, with a 70B model achieving only 2.78 tokens per second.

Given the massive 30 TB local NVMe SSD capacity and 1 TB of system memory, this instance offers high resource density for I/O-intensive operations. It is qualitatively cost-effective for workloads requiring high-throughput local storage and large memory footprints, eliminating the need for external storage attachments. The hardware profile is optimized for large-scale transactional databases, NoSQL databases, data warehousing, and high-performance caching layers like Redis.
description: Amazon Web Services i4i.32xlarge is a storage-optimized instance featuring 128 vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and 30,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, this x86_64 server delivers strong multi-core and database performance, evidenced by a Passmark CPU score of 86,632.57 and Redis SET throughput of 104.77 million operations per second. The system lacks dedicated GPUs, making it less suitable for large LLM generation tasks, but it excels in memory-intensive and high-I/O workloads. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for applications requiring massive local storage and high network throughput, which is supported by its 75 Gbps baseline bandwidth. This instance is highly suited for large-scale databases, data warehousing, and high-performance caching systems.
